about:
# BeastScout

A small World of Warcraft: Forever addon for hunters. Hover over a wild beast and its tooltip shows what you'd get by taming it:

- **Attack speed:** the swing timer your pet will have. In Forever that's set by the Faster/Slower Attack passive the beast comes with: Faster Attack I–VII gives 1.7, 1.6, 1.5, 1.4, 1.3, 1.2, 1.0; no passive gives 2.0. The tooltip names the passive, e.g. `1.3 (Faster Attack V, Handbook)`. Once a tame has listed a beast's skills and none of them is a speed passive, it shows `2.0 (no attack speed skill)`.
- **Teaches:** the exact ability ranks the beast teaches, including Faster/Slower Attack passives.
- **Family:** the abilities its family can learn and the pet level for each.
- **Diet:** what the family eats.
- **Pet food:** item tooltips say whether your summoned pet will eat it.
- **Upgrade for your pet:** if your current pet could use something the beast teaches, e.g. `Upgrade for Shal'ma: Bite 2 (has 1, 4 TP)`, or `Claw 3 (at pet level 16)` when your pet is too young. Only skills your pet's family can learn and that beat what it already knows are shown. Faster/Slower Attack never are: they only come with a tame.

Hover over your own pet to see its **loyalty**, **happiness** (and whether loyalty is rising) and **free training points**.

The extra lines only show up for hunters. No other addon is needed. It works on any client language: names from the game are matched by spell and map IDs, though BeastScout's own labels are in English.

## What it looks like

  ![A wild Ornery Galestrider's tooltip: attack speed 1.3 and Faster Attack 5, both from your own tame](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trevercomb/BeastScout/main/docs/screenshots/tooltip-tamed.png)
  ![A Shadowgale Ursera tooltip with an upgrade line for each pet: Claw 3 for Shalma and for River, at pet level 16](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trevercomb/BeastScout/main/docs/screenshots/tooltip-upgrade.png)

Hovering a beast shows its pet attack speed, what it teaches and where each value came from (left), and whether your current pet could use any of it (right).

![Your own pet's tooltip: loyalty Submissive (3 of 6), happiness Happy (loyalty rising), training points 12 free of 20 (30 at Dependable)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trevercomb/BeastScout/main/docs/screenshots/pet-tooltip.png)

Hovering your own pet shows its loyalty, happiness and training points, and what the next loyalty step is worth.

![The BeastScout window showing the best upgrades for a pet, grouped by skill, with Go buttons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trevercomb/BeastScout/main/docs/screenshots/window-upgrades.png)

`/beastscout` opens the window. Here: the best upgrades for a level 7 bear, grouped by skill, with the closest beasts first. Greyed rows are ranks the pet is too young for, and skills you've already learned say to train them at Beast Training.

![The world map with a BeastScout waypoint set on Loch Modan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trevercomb/BeastScout/main/docs/screenshots/map-waypoint.jpg)

Go (or a [Waypoint] link in chat) puts a waypoint on your map, and it clears itself when you get there.

## Where the data comes from

BeastScout's own data comes first; Hunter's Handbook only fills in what we haven't tracked yet. The tooltip says where each value came from, e.g. `1.5 (players, tamed x3)`.

1. **You:** what BeastScout recorded on your account but you haven't shared yet. It's used over the community data only when it's at least as reliable (a tame beats Beast Lore). Shown as `(you)`, `(you, tamed)` or `(you, Beast Lore)`.
   - **Taming:** right after Tame Beast, it reads your new pet's abilities, and its speed from its Faster/Slower Attack rank. This is the most reliable source. For two weeks after a tame BeastScout keeps checking that pet, and corrects the tame (and tells you) if its passive reads differently later.
   - **Beast Lore:** it reads ability ranks from the beast's tooltip after you cast Beast Lore. Since Forever's November 2026 patches, Beast Lore no longer lists a beast's skills, so in practice only tames add them now.
2. **Players:** BeastScout's own data in `Community.lua`: every observation we've accepted, including yours once shared. Shown with how it was observed and how many reports agree, e.g. `(players, tamed x3)`.
3. **Shared in game:** what other BeastScout players online found, shared automatically (see below). Used over the players' data only when it's more reliable. Shown as e.g. `(shared, tamed x2)`.
4. **Hunter's Handbook:** the fallback in `Handbook.lua`, 660 beasts converted from [Hunter's Handbook](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/hunters-handbook) by Wood (GPLv3). Thanks to them for the research. Shown as `(Handbook)`.

As players share more, the community data fills in and the fallback is needed less. `/beastscout help` shows how many beasts' skills and speeds hunters have shared so far, and each release's changelog notes the count.

Family abilities and diets are from [Seemeta](https://seemeta.com/en/wow-forever/pets), game version 1.60.1.

## Install

Copy this folder to `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\BeastScout`, so that `BeastScout.toc` sits directly inside it.

## The BeastScout window

Type `/beastscout` or click the minimap button (paw icon; drag it to move, `/beastscout minimap` hides it). The window has:

- a search box that takes anything `find` does: a skill (`bite 2`), a family (`cat`), `fast`, `fast cat`, `tank` or `upgrades`
- quick buttons for **Fastest**, **Tank**, **Upgrades for my pet** (beasts at your level that would teach your current pet something new) and **This zone** (beasts in your zone that would teach any of your pets something new)
- results with a **Go** button that sets a map waypoint; hover a row to see it in full
- **My pets** (each pet you've had out, with its skills, and Remove), **Pet stats** and **Export** buttons

It opens on your pet's upgrades when a pet is out, otherwise on the fastest beasts. If you use Daylight UI, the window takes its look: its window shell, fonts, buttons and colours. With EllesmereUI or ElvUI, the windows are skinned through their skinning APIs (EllesmereUI's can be turned off per addon in its options). This is new, so tell us if something looks off.

## Commands

Everything in the window also works in chat. `/bs` is a short form of `/beastscout` for every command (`/bs find tank`).

- `/beastscout`: opens the window. `/beastscout help` lists the commands and how many beasts each source covers.
- `/beastscout find upgrades`: beasts at your level that would teach your current pet something new. Grouped by skill: the best rank your pet can learn now from the 2 closest beasts (plus a weaker rank if it's closer), and, greyed, a higher rank within your level that your pet is too young for, with the pet level it needs. Shows training point costs. Skills you've already learned say **train it at Beast Training** instead of naming a beast: BeastScout reads the Beast Training window whenever you open it (Forever shows it in the class trainer window), and uses its pet level requirements over Hunter's Handbook's.
- `/beastscout zone`: beasts in the zone you're in, up to your level, that would teach any of your pets (the one out and every one you've had out) a rank it can't already get at Beast Training. Only the best rank of each skill found in the zone is listed, closest first, with waypoints; greyed ones need an older pet. BeastScout lists them on its own when you arrive in a zone (once per zone each session); `/beastscout zone auto` turns that off or on. Pets you haven't had out for 30 days are left out, here and in tooltips' upgrade lines (they stay in My pets).
- `/beastscout wish`: puts your target on your wishlist, or a beast by name (`/beastscout wish mystmane`); wishing again takes it off. Its nameplate then rings the rare alert, its tooltip says it's on your wishlist, and `/beastscout wishlist` lists them closest first (`/beastscout forget 2` removes row 2).
- `/beastscout vendors` (or `find food`): vendors you've visited that sell food your summoned pet eats, closest first, with waypoints. BeastScout remembers each vendor's food and drink when you open their window, and asks the game which of it your pet eats, so one visit covers every pet you'll have.
- `/beastscout find cat` (or `wolves`, `birds of prey`, ...): lists beasts of a family with their attack speed, closest first, with waypoints like below. `/beastscout find fast cat` sorts by speed instead, and plain `/beastscout find fast` lists the fastest beasts of any family.
- `/beastscout find tank`: tank families ranked by health and armor bonus (Bear, Boar, Turtle, ...), each with the closest beast you can tame. The bonuses are Classic's ([Highground Gaming](https://www.highgroundgaming.com/best-hunter-pets-in-wow-classic/)): Forever's aren't published, so BeastScout collects every player's pet readings (see `stats`) to work them out. The first readings varied more than family bonuses can explain (most likely the hunter's own gear counts too), so measured bonuses stay off until that's accounted for.
- `/beastscout stats`: your pets' health and armor as BeastScout measured them, by family and level (the lowest reading, so buffs don't count). They're shared with other players, and everyone's readings together give Forever's family bonuses for `find tank`.
- Find hides beasts above your level (and says how many). If none are tameable yet, it shows the lowest-level ones greyed out.
- `/beastscout find bite 2`: lists beasts that teach a skill (rank optional, Roman numerals work: `faster attack v`), ones you can tame at your level first, then closest to you, with zone and distance. Results are numbered; click [Waypoint] in chat or type `/beastscout way 2` to put a waypoint on the map. It clears itself when you get there.
- `/beastscout way Ashenvale 42.6 72.1`: found a beast's coordinates on a guide site, or one BeastScout doesn't know yet? This puts them on your map, no other addon needed (the start of a zone's name is enough: `way ashen 42.6 72.1`). Leave out the zone for the one you're in: `/beastscout way 42.6 72.1`. `/beastscout way clear` removes the waypoint.
- `/beastscout find mystmane`: finds beasts by name, or part of one (`find shal` finds Shal'ma), handy for rare spawns.
- `/beastscout find rares`: rare tameable beasts you (or bundled players) have seen. When a rare beast's nameplate (or one on your wishlist) shows up near you, BeastScout plays a sound and puts up a warning; rares that aren't in the Hunter's Handbook only get a quiet chat line, since they may not be tameable. Needs enemy nameplates on (V). `/beastscout alert` turns it off or on.
- `/beastscout export`: opens a window with your observations, ready to copy.
- `/beastscout food`: checks pet food for the item under your mouse (or `/beastscout food 117` for an item ID).
- `/beastscout pet`: shows what BeastScout reads from your current pet (spellbook, swing timer), and its health and armor next to your stamina and armor right now.
- `/beastscout debug`: reports each step of a tame in chat, for troubleshooting.
- `/beastscout reset`: forgets your observations.
- `/beastscout sharing`: turns in-game sharing off (or back on).
- `/beastscout share`: sends everything you've recorded now.
- `/beastscout forget shared`: forgets what other players shared.

## Sharing in game

Everyone running BeastScout shares automatically, guild or not, through hidden addon messages on a chat channel BeastScout joins for you (`BeastScoutData`, hidden from your chat windows). You don't need to wait for a release:

- Each new tame or Beast Lore finding goes out right away to every BeastScout player online on your virtual realm. Forever moves you between virtual realms as you change zones or join a party, and custom chat channels don't cross them, so live sharing reaches the players on yours (`/beastscout help` shows which one). What players agree on still reaches everyone through the bundled data in each update.
- When you log in, you send everything you've recorded, and a handful of players online (picked at random, so it stays light however many people use BeastScout) send theirs, so you catch up.
- Your own observations are sent, plus beasts at least two other players saw for themselves and agreed on, so findings keep spreading after the player who made them logs off. Passed-on data is never passed on again, counts half as much as a first-hand report, and shows as `(shared, passed on)`. Shared data stays out of `/beastscout export`.
- Your pets' measured health and armor are shared too (with the pet's family, level and loyalty, not its name, plus your own stamina and armor at the time, since pets seem to get part of their hunter's), so `find tank` can work out Forever's family bonuses. Pets of different levels are compared on a curve, and readings far off the rest (a debuff, say) are left out.
- Junk is dropped: unknown skills, impossible ranks or families. Each beast keeps the newest reports from up to 10 players. Reports are votes, with a tame counting more than Beast Lore, so one tame beats one Beast Lore but several players outvote a bad report. A level range far from what other players saw is left out.
- Shared data beats your own record only when at least two players saw it themselves.
- Saved shared data stays small: up to 2000 beasts (the least recently heard goes first), and a report nobody has sent for a year is dropped.
- Addon messages carry your character name like any chat, so BeastScout can count one report per player. `/beastscout sharing` turns it off and leaves the channel.
- If the channel can't be joined, BeastScout shares with your guild and group instead.

## Share your observations

Your observations improve everyone's tooltips once they're merged into a release.

1. In game, type `/beastscout export`. The text is already selected: press Ctrl+C.
2. Open [Share beast observations](https://github.com/trevercomb/BeastScout/issues/new?template=observations.yml) (needs a free GitHub account), paste, and submit. Your issue is deleted once its data is merged.

## Maintaining and forks

Forks are welcome. How shared observations are merged into the bundled data, and how releases are built and published, is in [docs/maintaining.md](https://github.com/trevercomb/BeastScout/blob/main/docs/maintaining.md).

## License

GPLv3, since BeastScout includes data from Hunter's Handbook. See `LICENSE`.

# BeastScout changelog

## 0.14.0

- New: arriving in a zone lists the beasts there that would teach any of your pets a rank it can't already get at Beast Training, closest first, with waypoints. Only the best rank of each skill in the zone is shown, and ranks your pets are too young for are greyed. It's shown once per zone each session; `/beastscout zone` (or **This zone** in the window) shows it any time, and `/beastscout zone auto` turns the arrival list off.
- Upgrade hints (in the zone list and beast tooltips) now skip pets you haven't had out for 30 days, so a pet you've let go stops cluttering them. Pets stay in My pets, and each one counts again once you summon it.
- New: a wishlist. `/beastscout wish` adds your target, or a beast by name (`/beastscout wish mystmane`); wishing again takes it off. A beast on your wishlist rings the rare alert when its nameplate shows up, even if it isn't rare, and its tooltip says it's on your wishlist. `/beastscout wishlist` lists them, closest first.
- New: `/beastscout vendors` (or `find food`) lists vendors you've visited that sell food your summoned pet eats, closest first, with waypoints. BeastScout remembers each vendor's food when you open their window and asks the game what your pet eats, so one visit covers all your pets.
- New from players' tames, many from Horde zones: The Rake (Faster Attack VI, 1.2), Thunderhawk Cloudscraper (Lightning Breath 2), Taloned Swoop (Demoralizing Screech 1), Greater Duskbat (Cower 1), Forest Moss Creeper (Bite 3) and Wildthorn Venomspitter (Web 2).
- Starving Mountain Lion stays Faster Attack VI: one tame that read a different rank no longer stops the others from filling in the passive a translated client missed.
- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 124 beasts (9 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 47 more.

## 0.13.16

- Fixed: on some translated clients (seen in Spanish and Russian), a tame could miss the beast's Faster Attack passive, so it was recorded with no attack speed skill and a speed of 2.0. BeastScout now also recognises the passive by its icon, so those tames get the right rank, and pets tamed in the last two weeks are corrected the next time they're out.
- `/beastscout pet` now also shows what BeastScout read from your pet's spellbook, so a passive it couldn't read is easy to spot.
- Starving Mountain Lion is settled again: Faster Attack VI (1.2) and Cower 2. Tames that missed the passive no longer count against the ones that saw it.
- New from players' tames: Elder Shadowmaw Panther (Faster Attack III, Dash 2, Prowl 2), Silt Crawler (Claw 6, Pinch 3), Bellygrub (Charge 3), Venom Web Spider (Web 1), Deepmoss Webspinner (Bite 3), Raging Reef Crawler (Pinch 1), and Foothills Duskbat (Sonic Blast 1), which the Hunter's Handbook never had.
- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 118 beasts (9 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 49 more.

## 0.13.15

- Fixed: since 0.11.0, BeastScout misread Faster Attack ranks on your pet. Faster Attack II and III were recorded a rank low and IV as V, so tames and shared data showed the wrong rank and attack speed. VI and VII, and Slower Attack, were always right.
- Your recorded tames and the shares you've heard are corrected once when you log in with this version. Shares from players still on older versions are corrected as they arrive, so updating is all you need to do. Where the old reading could have been either of two ranks, the Hunter's Handbook decides; if it doesn't know the beast, the reading stays as it was.
- Corrected: Coldrasp, Savannah Huntress, Juvenile Snow Leopard and Vulgara the Insatiable are Faster Attack III (1.5). Mountain Lion, Prairie Wolf Alpha, Prideclaw and Savannah Prowler are Faster Attack IV (1.4). Mystmane stays Faster Attack II (1.6).
- A fresh tame is now checked again after a reload, when you use `/beastscout pet`, and when your pet's spellbook updates, not only after a fight, so a wrong reading gets corrected sooner.
- New from players' tames: Elder Nightsaber (Faster Attack IV), Elmpaw (Claw 2) and Moss Stalker (Web 1).
- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 111 beasts (8 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 52 more.

## 0.13.14

- 34 more beasts from players' tames, many from Horde zones for the first time: Durotar Tiger, Ghostpaw Alpha, Ridge Stalker and Ridge Stalker Patriarch (Faster Attack V), Savannah Prowler (Faster Attack V; the Hunter's Handbook says IV), Savannah Huntress and Juvenile Snow Leopard (Faster Attack II), Venomtail Scorpid, Scorpid Hunter and Scorpashi Lasher (Scorpid Poison), Hecklefang Hyena (Tendon Rip 1), Fleeting Plainstrider (Dust Cloud 1), Worg (Furious Howl 1), Snapjaw (Shell Shield 1), and more.
- New beasts the Handbook had no skills for: Wildplains Patriarch (Faster Attack V, Cower 4), Giant Grizzled Bear (Swipe 1), Highland Raptor (Savage Rend 2), Young Wetlands Crocolisk (Dismember 1), Sootfur (Bite 5) and Swoop (Claw 1).
- Starving Mountain Lion is settled: three tames agree on Faster Attack VI (1.2) and Cower 2.
- Mystmane is back to Faster Attack II (1.6), checked in a tamed pet's spellbook and swing timer. Tames recorded before 0.13.13 had caught the game showing Faster Attack I right after taming.
- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 108 beasts (8 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 51 more.

## 0.13.13

- Right after a tame, the game sometimes shows a lower Faster or Slower Attack rank than the pet really has. BeastScout now remembers the beast each new pet came from, and if the pet's spellbook later shows a different rank within two weeks, it corrects that beast's skills and speed, tells you in chat, and shares the fix.
- Mystmane on Zephras Isle corrected to Faster Attack II (1.6), matching the Hunter's Handbook. Its tame first showed Faster Attack I.
- Your pet readings now include your own stamina and armor, so the measured family bonuses for `/beastscout find tank` can take your gear out once enough readings come in. `/beastscout pet` shows both your pet's and your own current numbers.
- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 74 beasts (6 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 58 more.

## 0.13.12

- `/beastscout find tank` is back to Classic's numbers. The first pet readings players shared varied far more than family bonuses can explain (most likely your own gear counts toward your pet's health and armor), so measured bonuses could rank families wrongly. Readings are still collected and shared, so they can return once that's accounted for.
- New from a player's tame: Mystmane, the rare bear on Zephras Isle, teaches Faster Attack I (1.7) and Swipe 1. The Hunter's Handbook says Faster Attack II.
- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 74 beasts (6 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 58 more.

## 0.13.11

- Your pets' health and armor are now shared with other BeastScout players (family, level and loyalty, not the pet's name), to work out Forever's family bonuses, which aren't published. Once enough pets are measured, `/beastscout find tank` ranks families by what was measured in Forever, shown as e.g. `measured, 12 pets`, and can rank Fox, Bird of Prey and Core Hound too. Until then it uses Classic's numbers, as before.
- New from players' tames: Mountain Lion (Faster Attack V, Prowl 1), Needles Cougar (Faster Attack VI), Bloodsnout Worg (Bite 3) and Webwood Silkspinner (Bite 2). Coyote, Scarred Crag Boar and Sunscale Screecher now list their skills.
- `/beastscout help` describes `/beastscout way` as what it's for: putting a beast's coordinates from a guide on your map.
- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 72 beasts (6 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 59 more.

## 0.13.8

# BeastScout changelog

## 0.13.15

- Fixed: since 0.11.0, BeastScout misread Faster Attack ranks on your pet. Faster Attack II and III were recorded a rank low and IV as V, so tames and shared data showed the wrong rank and attack speed. VI and VII, and Slower Attack, were always right.
- Your recorded tames and the shares you've heard are corrected once when you log in with this version. Shares from players still on older versions are corrected as they arrive, so updating is all you need to do. Where the old reading could have been either of two ranks, the Hunter's Handbook decides; if it doesn't know the beast, the reading stays as it was.
- Corrected: Coldrasp, Savannah Huntress, Juvenile Snow Leopard and Vulgara the Insatiable are Faster Attack III (1.5). Mountain Lion, Prairie Wolf Alpha, Prideclaw and Savannah Prowler are Faster Attack IV (1.4). Mystmane stays Faster Attack II (1.6).
- A fresh tame is now checked again after a reload, when you use `/beastscout pet`, and when your pet's spellbook updates, not only after a fight, so a wrong reading gets corrected sooner.
- New from players' tames: Elder Nightsaber (Faster Attack IV), Elmpaw (Claw 2) and Moss Stalker (Web 1).
- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 111 beasts (8 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 52 more.

- New beasts the Handbook had no skills for: Wildplains Patriarch (Faster Attack V, Cower 4), Giant Grizzled Bear (Swipe 1), Highland Raptor (Savage Rend 2), Young Wetlands Crocolisk (Dismember 1), Sootfur (Bite 5) and Swoop (Claw 1).
- Starving Mountain Lion is settled: three tames agree on Faster Attack VI (1.2) and Cower 2.
- Mystmane is back to Faster Attack II (1.6), checked in a tamed pet's spellbook and swing timer. Tames recorded before 0.13.13 had caught the game showing Faster Attack I right after taming.
- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 108 beasts (8 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 51 more.

- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 72 beasts (6 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 59 more.

## 0.13.8

- With EllesmereUI or ElvUI installed, the BeastScout and export windows are skinned to match, through their skinning APIs. EllesmereUI can turn this off per addon under Blizzard Skins+ > Window Skins > Third-Party Addons. This is new and lightly tested, so please report anything that looks wrong. Without them, nothing changes.
- Sharing is harder to fool. Reports are now votes, with a tame counting more than Beast Lore: one tame still beats one Beast Lore, but a single bad report can no longer outvote several players. A level range far from what other players saw is left out.

- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 54 beasts (5 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 58 more.

- Fixed: a tame that was interrupted or failed, followed by calling your own pet back within a minute, could record your pet's skills as the wild beast's.

- Fixed: if adding BeastScout's lines to a tooltip ever failed, it kept retrying and could pile up partial lines.
- Fixed: a beast targeted in combat could fail to record when its name or level was hidden.
- Sharing is safer: a malformed share can no longer store a beast ID your saved data can't load back, and shared beast names can't carry icons, links or colours.
- Bundled data: Savannah Patriarch's Cower 4 is back to the Hunter's Handbook's Cower 2 until a second player's tame confirms it.
- Hunters like you have now shared skills and speeds for 54 beasts (5 the Handbook never had), plus spawn points for 58 more.
